title: Introduce hermetic Go CI runtime and slimline pipeline shim
author: Ava Chen
description: Motivation: our existing CI relies on many small shell scripts invoked from workflow YAMLs; those scripts are a common source of subtle failures (environment differences, word-splitting bugs, silent pipefail issues) and make local dev/CI parity hard. This change introduces a small hermetic Go-based CI runtime (ci-runner) that replaces the most fragile shell entrypoints and consolidates common plumbing (workspace setup, action inputs normalization, token-safe logging, artifact staging). Goals: (1) reduce flakes by making CI entrypoints deterministic, (2) shrink workflow YAMLs to declarative stages and let the runner handle retries/backoff, (3) centralize action pinning and dependency-check hooks, and (4) pave way for incremental migration of legacy jobs. Work in this PR: - Add tools/ci/runner/main.go (single binary ~7 file packages) that implements: workspace bootstrap, env validation, action pin checks, optional sandboxing flags, and a small plugin interface for short-lived job steps. - Replace top-level shell scripts used by heavy integration lanes with thin shims that invoke ci-runner (scripts retained for compatibility during rollout). - Update .github/workflows/ci.yml to call the runner with structured inputs and reduce ad-hoc step logic. - Introduce tools/ci/runner/go.mod and minimal Dockerfile for hermetic images used by self-hosted runners. - Pin a handful of GitHub Actions SHAs and add action-compatibility guard that logs warning when an action input signature changes. - Add a lightweight dep-health check that warns (non-blocking) for transitive devdeps introduced by dependency bumps. Rollout plan: 1) Merge to main behind a feature flag (CI flag: USE_HERMETIC_RUNNER=true) so all jobs continue to run in parallel with legacy shells for two cycles. 2) Monitor flaky-test rate, CI median runtime, and failed step entropy for 3 consecutive releases. 3) Flip default flag, keep legacy shims for 30 days as a hotfix rollback path. 4) Remove legacy scripts after telemetry validates stability. Checklist: - [x] add go runner source and minimal tests - [x] update CI workflows to call runner - [x] pin key GH Actions SHAs - [x] add documentation in tools/ci/runner/README.md - [x] smoke test on release branch - [x] add linear tickets for follow-ups (ENG-4872, ENG-4924) Related work: smaller follow-ups will move lint and release signing steps into the runner as plugins (see ENG-4901). Backwards compatibility: runner accepts legacy envs and exits with non-zero codes on malformed inputs so current workflows that rely on exit codes still behave the same. Migration notes for on-call and SRE are in tools/ci/runner/README.md.

change_summary: Replace several fragile shell entrypoints with a single hermetic Go-based CI runner, pin key GH Actions, add dep-health gating, and slim workflow YAMLs.

monitor flaky-test rate and runner.step_retries metric

release_notes: developer-facing: Introduces a hermetic Go CI runner to replace fragile shell entrypoints. No user-facing product changes. Ops: follow rollout plan and watch CI telemetry.
